definition: Hemoglobin A1c measures the percentage of hemoglobin coated with sugar, reflecting average blood glucose over the past 2–3 months.

definition: Postprandial glucose measures blood sugar 1–2 hours after a meal, reflecting how well your body processes carbohydrates.

definition: Total cholesterol is the combined amount of LDL, HDL, and VLDL in your blood; used as an initial cardiovascular risk screening value.

guideline_citations.ACC_AHA: Grundy SM, et al. 2018 AHA/ACC Guideline on Management of Blood Cholesterol. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2019;73(24):e285-e350. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2018.11.003

definition: LDL (“bad”) cholesterol drives arterial plaque buildup; lowering it is the primary goal of cholesterol-lowering therapy.

guideline_citations.ACC_AHA: Grundy SM, et al. 2018 AHA/ACC Guideline on Management of Blood Cholesterol. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2019;73(24):e285-e350. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2018.11.003

definition: HDL (“good”) cholesterol transports excess cholesterol back to the liver; higher levels are generally protective against heart disease.

guideline_citations.ACC_AHA: Grundy SM, et al. 2018 AHA/ACC Guideline on Management of Blood Cholesterol. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2019;73(24):e285-e350. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2018.11.003

definition: Triglycerides are blood fats stored from unused calories; elevated levels are linked to metabolic syndrome and cardiovascular risk.

guideline_citations.ACC_AHA: Grundy SM, et al. 2018 AHA/ACC Guideline on Management of Blood Cholesterol. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2019;73(24):e285-e350. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2018.11.003

provenance.notes: Measured fasting for most accurate results

definition: Non-HDL cholesterol (total minus HDL) captures all atherogenic lipoproteins and is a more comprehensive cardiovascular risk marker than LDL alone.

guideline_citations.ACC_AHA: Grundy SM, et al. 2018 AHA/ACC Guideline on Management of Blood Cholesterol. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2019;73(24):e285-e350. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2018.11.003

provenance.notes: Calculated as Total Cholesterol minus HDL-C

definition: eGFR (estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate) estimates how much blood your kidneys filter per minute — the primary measure of kidney function.

guideline_citations.ADA: American Diabetes Association. Standards of Care in Diabetes—2024. Diabetes Care. 2024;47(Suppl 1):S1-S321. https://doi.org/10.2337/dc24-S001

definition: Creatinine is a muscle-metabolism waste product filtered by the kidneys; elevated blood levels signal reduced kidney function.

provenance.notes: Reference ranges vary by lab; used to calculate eGFR

definition: Urine Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratio measures albumin leaking into urine — an early indicator of kidney damage from diabetes or hypertension.

guideline_citations.ADA: American Diabetes Association. Standards of Care in Diabetes—2024. Diabetes Care. 2024;47(Suppl 1):S1-S321. https://doi.org/10.2337/dc24-S001

provenance.notes: Spot urine sample; preferred over 24h collection

definition: Systolic blood pressure is the peak arterial pressure when your heart contracts; it is the top number in a blood pressure reading.

definition: Diastolic blood pressure is the arterial pressure between heartbeats; it is the bottom number in a blood pressure reading.

guideline_citations.ACC_AHA: Whelton PK, et al. 2017 ACC/AHA Hypertension Guideline. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2018;71(19):e127-e248. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2017.11.006

definition: High-sensitivity CRP measures low-grade systemic inflammation; levels above 2 mg/L signal elevated cardiovascular risk even within conventional normal ranges.

definition: Vitamin B12 is essential for nerve function and red blood cell production; deficiency can occur with metformin use or inadequate dietary intake.

guideline_citations.WHO: WHO. Haemoglobin concentrations for the diagnosis of anaemia and assessment of severity. WHO/NMH/NHD/MNM/11.1. https://www.who.int/vmnis/indicators/haemoglobin/en/

Albumin is the most abundant plasma protein, produced by the liver; low levels indicate malnutrition, liver disease, or chronic illness.
Total globulin reflects immune proteins in the blood; elevated levels may indicate infection, inflammation, or liver disease.
The A/G ratio compares albumin to globulin; a low ratio can indicate overproduction of globulins (as in multiple myeloma) or underproduction of albumin (as in liver disease).
Total protein measures the combined concentration of albumin and globulins; used to assess nutritional status and liver and kidney function.
Alkaline phosphatase is a liver and bone enzyme; elevated levels can indicate liver disease, bile duct obstruction, or bone disorders.
Total bilirubin measures the breakdown product of red blood cells processed by the liver; elevated levels indicate jaundice, liver disease, or hemolysis.
Serum calcium reflects bone metabolism, parathyroid function, and kidney health; abnormal levels are linked to bone disease, kidney stones, and endocrine disorders.
Total CO2 (bicarbonate) reflects the body's acid-base balance; low values indicate metabolic acidosis, high values indicate alkalosis or COPD compensation.
VLDL carries triglycerides from the liver to tissues; elevated VLDL is associated with cardiovascular risk.
Hepatitis B surface antibody indicates immunity to HBV, either from vaccination or prior infection.
Qualitative assessment of urine clarity; normal is clear.
Qualitative assessment of urine color; normal is yellow.
Urine pH measures acidity; normal range is 4.5–8.0.
Specific gravity measures urine concentration; normal range is 1.001–1.030.
Qualitative urine protein screen; persistent positivity may indicate kidney disease.
Qualitative urine glucose; normally absent, presence may indicate diabetes.
Qualitative urine ketone screen; elevated in diabetic ketoacidosis or starvation.
Qualitative urine blood screen; positive results may indicate hematuria, kidney stones, or infection.
Qualitative nitrite screen; positive indicates bacterial infection (UTI).
Qualitative leukocyte esterase screen; positive suggests white blood cells in urine, indicating infection or inflammation.
Qualitative urine bilirubin; normally absent, presence may indicate liver disease.

provenance.notes: qualitative — disambiguated from serum bilirubin by absent unit
